What does Russia mean by 1997? The year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, that “green premium” remains important, but it is no longer the only consideration. Commercial priorities, geopolitical pressures and government policies increasingly shape investment decisions and the shift towards lower-carbon alternatives.A low-carbon product can cost more but still be the smarter business choiceAs a result, a low-carbon product can cost more but still be the smarter business choice. Companies investing in clean technologies must therefore weigh a broader set of factors, including volatile energy and material costs, value chain resilience, market opportunities and risks, government policies affecting industrial competitiveness, and their positioning in the low-carbon economy.
